pageCache.text:
Church of England Primary School · Stockwell, SW9
Your local first class school.All day, every day.
One class in every year group, so every child is known by name — and a school day that runs from 7.30am to 6pm, so it works around yours.
For families — the things you came here for
We have places available now — in Reception and in most other year groups. Moving into the area, or thinking about a change? Call the office on 020 7274 7012 and we will tell you straight away what we have.
Three reasons families choose St Andrew's
We are a small school in the middle of Stockwell, and we have built the things around that which working families in this part of Lambeth actually need.
A school day that fits round yours
Breakfast Club from 7.30am, the school day from 8.55 to 3.30, after-school activities until 4.30 and our Cabin Club until 6pm. One of the longest school days in Lambeth, every day of the week — and you only use it when you need it.
Small enough to know every child
One class in each year group, with a maximum of thirty in Reception. Every teacher knows every child, and most of the staff know their families too. That is a deliberate choice, and we intend to keep it.
Recognised, independently, ten times over
Inclusion, the arts, wellbeing, work with more able children, religious education, our partnership with parents — all assessed and awarded by organisations outside the school. Not our opinion of ourselves.
The day at St Andrew's
From breakfast to the end of your working day, in one place, with people who know your child.
Sport, art, music, clubs, structured and unstructured play — and quiet time too. You might need the early start twice a week, or the late pick-up once a term. It is there either way.
Times, activities and costs
Judged good, and recently
Read the full inspection report on the Ofsted website, and our church school inspection outcome on our SIAMS page.
Ten independent awards
Each of these was assessed by an organisation outside the school. Together they say more about St Andrew's than anything we could write ourselves.
Come and see us
Nobody chooses a school from a website. Three ways to have a proper look, and you are welcome to do all three.
A school tour
Half an hour with a member of staff, during the school day, so you see the classrooms while the children are in them. Ask us anything.
Stay & Play
Bring your child and let them join in. The best way to see whether they settle here — and most of the time, they do not want to leave.
A 3D tour, from home
Walk through the whole school on your phone, at eleven o'clock at night, in your own time. Then come and see the real thing.
A word from our headteacher
At St Andrew's we welcome you to our happy, safe and Christian family, where we encourage everyone to do their very best.
Our vision is to inspire our children to be confident individuals, who are excited about learning and curious about the world they live in. It is our desire that every child who joins St Andrew's will achieve high academic standards and, as our school motto says, reach for the stars — and beyond.
Jayne MitchellExecutive Headteacher, SW9 Partnership
Read the full welcome
Applying for a place
Three steps, and we will help you with all of them. If you are applying mid-year, skip straight to the phone call.
Come and visit
Book a tour or a Stay & Play. We will explain how the Lambeth application system works and answer every question you have.
Apply through Lambeth
Reception places are allocated by your local council, not by us. Applications for September 2027 close at midnight on 15 January 2027.
Tell us you have applied
Let the office know and we will make sure everything on our side is in order. One phone call or email is enough.
This school is for everyone
St Andrew's is a Church of England school, and we are an inclusive school that welcomes all learners regardless of race, gender, ethnicity or religion, stage of English learning, ability, special educational needs or impairments. We are proud of the values that underpin our Christian school, and we encourage applications from families of all faiths and of none.
We currently have places, so all applications are being accepted. Our full admissions policy, including the criteria that would apply if the school were oversubscribed, is available here.
Help, when you need it
Every family hits a patch where something is harder than usual. Nobody here will think less of you for asking, and most of what we can help with costs nothing at all.
Inclusion and SEND
If your child needs extra help, or you think they might, talk to us early. We will walk you through what happens next and who does what.
Wellbeing
What we do in school to look after how children feel, and where to turn if things are hard at home too.
Helping at home
Reading, spellings, times tables and the rest — practical things that make a difference, without turning your evening into a battle.
The PTA
Discos, fairs, cake and fundraising. Come to one thing and see — there is no expectation to join a committee.
Find us, and talk to us
Contact page and full details
Visit our Classes

Executive Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to our small, successful and happy church primary school, recognised by Ofsted as good with an outstanding curriculum.
St Andrew’s is a very welcoming school and we are known for our friendly, family atmosphere.
We have excellent relationships with our families and know our children very well – one of the many advantages of being a small school.
Our aim is to ensure that every pupil enjoys their time at St Andrew’s and develops a lively and enquiring mind.
We value each and every child as an individual and encourage their unique development whilst emphasising the importance of respect, team work, responsibility and hard work.
I know that your son or daughter will flourish at St Andrew’s. During their time with us we will encourage them to become confident and independent learners who reach for the stars.
Please come and visit us soon – I look forward to meeting you.
Executive Headteacher

PSHE and Citizenship
Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE) prepares all the pupils for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of life.
PSHE is a combination of a taught lesson and all the activities that contribute to pupils' personal and social development, e.g. Health elements within science, circle time, school council, community service and helping other children with their work and behaviour.

After School Clubs
St Andrew’s after school activities are available every day of the school year and are open to all pupils.
Our Lambeth after school programmes are in response to the needs of busy parents and carers who need a safe, friendly and creative environment with quality childcare for those extra few hours at the end of the school day.
We know how the average working day doesn’t fit with the school day – that’s why there’s nothing average about our after school sessions!
All children who come to St Andrew’s after school activities are encouraged to take part in a wide range of activities in a friendly, safe, sociable and welcoming environment.
School Finishes : 3:30pm
After School Activities : 3:30pm – 4:30pm
Snack for ‘Cabin Club’ pupils : 4:30pm
St Andrew’s After School Activities and After School ‘Cabin Club’
At St Andrews you have the option of childcare from the end of the standard school day up until 6:00pm, and you can collect your child at any point during the after school programme.
We break this extended after school care into two sections:
BOOK After School Activities (3.30 - 4.30pm) HERE
Book After School Club (3.30 - 6pm) HERE
After School Activities from 3:30pm until 4:30pm
St Andrew’s After School Activities
At 3:30pm all children staying for any of the after school programme meet in the hall and we take a first register. The activities that begin after the end of the school day offer a whole range of structured options for your child that are creative, stimulating and fun which take place both indoors and outside, weather permitting. Activities are led by specialist tutors and our own staff.
Below is an example of the range of activities that are on offer after school:
Your child is free to try any of the activities on offer and can take part in different activities on different days of the week. All activities change on a term-by-term basis to ensure variety and exciting options for your children.
Art
Dance
Gymnastics
Football
Basketball
St Andrew’s After School Cabin Club
For those children staying longer, our After School ‘Cabin Club’ operates once After School Activities have finished. Cabin Club runs from 4:30pm until 6:00pm every day, and includes a healthy nutritious snack for all the children.
All the children who are staying for Cabin Club head to our Portakabin (see where we got the name from?) at 4:30pm where we take a further register. Then they’ll all have a snack before spending the rest of the session in free play indoors or outdoors, as a final chance to unwind.
All children must be collected by 6:00pm at the latest.
After school snacks at Cabin Club
ll children who stay for Cabin Club are provided with a healthy and nutritious snack at 4:30pm.
We change the snack daily and you can see a sample weekly menu below:
Monday: Bagels with various toppings.Tuesday: Sandwiches with various fillings.Wednesday: PizzaThursday: Tomato pasta with cheese & Fruit.Friday: Croissants with Jam & Fruit.
How does St Andrew’s After School Activities and Cabin Club work?
St Andrew’s after school activities are available every day or on a one-off basis. We do ask that you book in advance, but will do our best to accommodate last minute ‘on the day’ requests whenever possible.
You can choose just the After School Activities (until 4:30pm) or you can opt to add Cabin Club as well (until 6:00pm) and you can make payments as set out below.
Booking: You need to book After School Activities and Cabin Club in advance with the school office.
Time: 3:30pm – 6:00pm
Costs: After School Activities (until 4:30pm) - £5.00 per day. After School Activities plus Cabin Club (until 6:00pm) - £14.00 per day All after school childcare fees can be paid via Parent Pay or with Childcare Vouchers.
Important: You can choose to have your child attend After School Activities on its own or add on Cabin Club.
All children must be collected by 6:00pm.
If you’re a prospective parent and haven’t had a school tour yet, please arrange one asap here so you can learn more about the extended school day:

Breakfast Club
St Andrew’s Breakfast Club is available every day of the school year and is open to all pupils from 7:30am.
Breakfast club : 7:30 – 9am
School opens : 8:45am
School Registration : 8:55am
Book BREAKFAST CLUB HERE
We know what it’s like for many parents and carers first thing in the morning with a hectic rush to get out of the house and get everyone to school.
That’s why we aim to provide you with a full day of childcare and education in a safe and welcoming environment for your child – starting with an early drop off and a healthy and nutritious breakfast for your child.
‘Your local first class school - all day, every day’
The standard opening time for St Andrews is 8:45am, but Breakfast Club allows a drop off from 7:30am.
Children are offered breakfast on arrival to get them ready for a busy day of learning and fun. A choice of cereals, yoghurts, rice cakes and raisins are available daily, along with a choice of hot and cold breakfasts and drinks from the following:
After eating breakfast the children have the choice to play with their friends (with access to the playground under supervision), or take part in structured activities, such as reading, drawing, arts and crafts, board games, lego or circle time and more.
Children attending Breakfast Club are then taken directly to class in time for the beginning of the school day at 9am.
‘I love breakfast club. The food is yummy and I love playing with my friends before school starts.’ Year 3 pupil.
Choice of cereals and milk
Cheese toasties
Baked Beans or scrambled eggs on toast
Bagels with a choice of toppings
How does St Andrew’s Breakfast Club work?
St Andrew’s Breakfast Club is available every day or on a one-off basis and you do not need to book in advance.
Simply turn up on the days you wish your child to join Breakfast Club and make payments as set out below.
Booking: Book your place at Breakfast Club HERE
Costs: £4.50 per session. Breakfast Club can be paid via Parent Pay or with Childcare Vouchers.
Important: Children must arrive at school by 8:30am at the latest to be on time for Breakfast Club but should not arrive before 7:30am.

Collective Worship
We work closely with the Southwark Diocesan Board of Education who provide support and an advisory service to the Head teacher and staff.
Our vicar regularly visits the school to lead assemblies and the children visit the church once or twice each term.
All staff encourage and welcome the involvement of parents in the Religious Education of their children and the prayer life of the school.
Parents are kept informed of events in a weekly newsletter and are always invited to join us for our celebrations in church.
Collective Worship/Assemblies are held every day in the hall for the whole school, or in Key Stage groups or in classrooms.
Time for prayer, reflection and celebration is given in a conductive atmosphere.
Assemblies are also time for giving children information and talking about school issues.
On occasion, throughout the year our children lead an assembly to which the parents are invited to attend.
Our last RE Inspection was in March 2019 when we were judged as an EXCELLENT school.
You can download the report below:St Andrews Stockwell Section 48 Inspection Report

Our Governors
William Garrood - Chair of Governors
I have been a St Andrew's governor since 2016 and chair since 2020. I am a church governor, but also a parent, with two boys at the school in year 3 and 6. They've both been there since reception. It’s been a great school for them for the formal side and for helping them feel happy and safe.
Originally, I’m from just outside London, but I’ve lived in London since 2000. For the first few years in north London (where I was also a school governor) and in Stockwell since 2006. I believe education and the role of schools is critical for our children and really helps bring communities together.
I am currently the Director of Strategy for WaterAid, a development charity dedicated to water, sanitation and hygiene. I aim to bring my expertise in governance and performance to the governing body to help the staff do the best job for all the children.
William Scoones - Vice Chair of Governors
Enter your text here...
Jayne Mitchell - Executive Headteacher
I qualified as a teacher in 1991 and worked in Islington for many years before I was appointed as the Headteacher at St. Andrew's in 2002. In 2016 our school partnered with Christ Church SW9 and I was appointed as the Executive Headteacher of the federation. Over the years, I have been a serving Ofsted inspector, I have chaired many Lambeth committees and working groups and I am currently a member of the Lambeth Schools Partnership Board.
I am passionate about education and the development of our children as individuals who can make informed choices. I believe strongly in growing academic skills and knowledge, but also believe in physical, personal and creative development. School is about improving skills and knowledge, developing friendships, learning how to be good citizens, having fun and growing independence. It is an absolute privilege to be the Headteacher at St. Andrew's and to work with all our amazing children and families.
Anne-Marie Spring - Staff Governor

Music
At St. Andrews we are proud of the enthusiasm that our children have about music and we enjoy celebrating this throughout each academic year in performances, assemblies, collective worship, concerts and church services.
Every class has a weekly music lesson which is taught by our music teacher.
In line with the National Curriculum, we believe that a high-quality music education should engage and inspire our children to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement.
Our children are given many opportunities to compose, listen, perform and appraise, as well as to apply their understanding of the dimensions of music as they refine their skills in these.
Click here to see our MUSIC CURRICULUM MAP
During their time at St. Andrew's, our children also have the opportunity to perform annually in school concerts, church services and class assemblies. They learn songs in a variety of styles and even in different languages!
In addition, some of our classes take part in Lambeth Music Festival at the Royal Festival Hall, sing in a Gospel choir concert 'The Big Sing' at St. Gabriel's College and participate in services at Southwark Cathedral.
It is not only the Creative Arts (singing, dancing and drama) that our children have the opportunity to develop their skills in; they can also learn to play a wide variety of musical instruments.

Science
Our Vision
Our vision at St. Andrew’s is to inspire our children to be excited about learning and curious about the world they live in.
We aim to provide a science curriculum which offers the children the opportunity to think scientifically and explore the world so that they have a deeper knowledge and understanding of a range of scientific concepts.
Science lessons aim to nurture children’s curiosity through practical hands-on experiences that inspire questions and inquiry.

How do we plan and teach science?
A science unit is taught every half term. Teachers plan sequences of lessons across the unit that will build on and develop the children’s knowledge and skills.
Each unit of learning has a strong foundation in new knowledge, linked to prior knowledge, that will support the children to understand increasingly complex scientific phenomena and processes.
Scientific vocabulary is mapped and taught rigorously to ensure that children can both recognise, understand and use scientific terminology accurately and confidently.
Opportunities to learn outdoors and explore our natural environment are embedded throughout our science curriculum.
Carefully selected skills are planned to best match each unit of knowledge and progress year on year.
Opportunities to practise and embed skills are planned for so that they are revisited and refined over time.
The knowledge and skills that children will develop throughout each science topic are mapped across each year group and across the school to ensure progression.
How do we evaluate learning in science?
The impact of our science curriculum can be seen in the children's books, by talking with the children and through our environment.
At the beginning of each unit, a detailed overview outlines the main learning objective alongside the skills that the children will build on and those which will follow.
Children also complete a KWL grid which they revisit at the end of the unit.
Class teachers then use the children's class learning and assessments, along with observations of their skills when carrying out experiments and investigations, to make a judgement as to whether each child is working towards, at or above the expected level.

Our Curriculum
At St. Andrew’s our vision is to inspire our children to be confident individuals, who are excited about learning and curious about the world they live in.
We want our children to come to school every day eager to learn new things, confident to try new experiences and enthusiastic about new challenges.
We want each child to experience success and to leave us at the end of primary school as caring, thoughtful citizens who are ambitious for themselves and fully prepared for secondary school.
We intend to achieve this by providing a well-planned and ambitious curriculum that reflects our local community and the heritage of our children and their families. We serve a diverse and vibrant community who speak many languages and come from many different parts of the world and this is reflected throughout our curriculum.
Our curriculum provides opportunities for our children to celebrate their local area and to understand its geography and history.
It takes them beyond their immediate local context as they learn about the city of London and the wider study of the UK, and further afield, as they learn about what it means to be a global citizen.
Our study of the history, geography, music and artwork of countries around the world is intended to help our children see that which lies outside of their personal experiences.
In subjects such as art, design technology and music, we place a high emphasis both on creativity and technical skill.
We want our children to have the knowledge and skills they need to appreciate works of great art, music and architecture and create, compose and construct works of their own.
All children have the opportunity to learn a musical instrument and we regularly work in partnership with professional artists and musicians.
In RE our children are encouraged to develop and express their own beliefs and values.
They are taught about other religions and customs that may be different from their own.
Our PSHE lessons are also important spaces for learning about difference and how to be respectful and tolerant citizens.
In science, we build on our children’s innate curiosity and help them make sense of the world around them both through the explicit teaching and through guided experimentation and observation.
We take every opportunity to use our local surroundings for rich learning experiences.
We have a strong emphasis on teaching the basic skills of reading, writing and maths to the highest standard so that our children can achieve their full potential and to reach for the stars.
We have placed the development of language at the heart of our curriculum which is designed to ensure that our children develop into confident speakers, readers and writers.
Our aim is for our children to develop a real love for books and that they take this passion with them into adulthood.
We also want our children to leave us as confident mathematicians, with numerical fluency and flexible problem-solving strategies that help them navigate the world around them and which open doors to other areas of learning.
Finally, we believe that our children should grow up to be caring citizens who are thoughtful and respectful not just of each other but also of the world around them.
Our school holds six core values and they are at the heart of all that we do. These values are faithfulness, joy, kindness, peace, love and perseverance.
Our values are woven throughout our curriculum and in every subject we seek opportunities to explore what it means to be kind, caring, thoughtful and respectful citizens.
Our curriculum has been developed by staff after careful analysis and reflection of the needs of our children.
We have thought carefully about the places in the world we want our children to learn about, the events that will capture their imagination and the important knowledge, skills and understanding we want them to have by the time they leave us.
We promote enjoyment for learning and encourage children to be independent, reflective learners through the development of thinking skills.

Our Vision and Values
At St. Andrew's we welcome you to our happy, safe and Christian family, where we encourage everyone to do their very best. Our vision is to inspire our children to be confident individuals, who are excited about learning and curious about the world they live in. It is our desire that every child who joins St. Andrew’s will achieve high academic standards and indeed, as our school motto states ‘Reach for the Stars’ and beyond!
Biblical Foundation - I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly. (John 10:10)
Our vision reflects a Christian understanding of God - We believe in a loving, creating, and empowering God who knows each person individually. This inspires our educational mission to nurture every child's God-given potential, seek academic excellence, and provide teaching of the highest possible standard within a Christian family environment.
Our vision reflects our belief about ourselves and each other - We believe that every child and adult in our community is uniquely created in the image of God, precious, and deserving of the very best. From an educational perspective, this drives our commitment to personal and academic flourishing. We aim to enable pupils to develop confidence, independence, lively enquiring minds, high standards of personal conduct, and a strong sense of self-worth.
It reflects our belief about the world - We believe we are called to live well together in harmony and stewardship. We encourage our children to be curious about the world they live in, to develop questioning skills, and to build the knowledge and resilience needed to meet the challenges of everyday life with hope.
Our Vision in practice
We live out our vision and values in active partnership with parents and the wider community by:
Our school holds six core values that sit at the absolute heart of everything we do: kindness, peace, perseverance, faithfulness, love, and joy.
Our vision and these values are inextricably linked, working seamlessly together to shape our daily life, our curriculum, and our community. Deeply rooted in Christian teachings, this alignment ensures that our academic aspirations and spiritual growth are anchored in faith, inspiring every child to live out these values as they 'Reach for the Stars' and beyond.
KINDNESS (Ephesians 4:32 – 'Instead, be kind to each other, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, just as God through Christ has forgiven you.')
Our commitment to a warm welcome and high standards of behaviour mirrors Ephesians 4:32. We make kindness an active daily practice by valuing each person's contributions, supporting our peers, and fostering a forgiving, compassionate environment where everyone feels respected.
PEACE (2 Thessalonians 3:16 – 'May the Lord of peace give you peace always in everything. The Lord will be with you all.')
Providing a safe and secure learning environment directly reflects the blessing of 'peace always in everything' (2 Thessalonians 3:16). This deep, God-given tranquility removes anxiety, creating the foundation that inspires our pupils to become confident individuals who feel free to take risks in their learning.
PERSEVERANCE (2 Thessalonians 3:13 – 'But you, friends, must not become tired of doing right.')
Reaching beyond the stars demands resilience, which is why we equip pupils to handle the challenges of everyday life. This aligns with 2 Thessalonians 3:13's call to not become tired of doing right. Working in active partnership, our children never work alone; together, we find the strength to persevere and keep striving for our best.
FAITHFULNESS (Proverbs 3:3 – 'Let love and faithfulness never leave you, bind them around your neck, and write them on the tablet of your heart.')
Challenging everyone to do their very best requires steadfast dedication. Proverbs 3:3 urges us to write faithfulness 'on the tablet of your heart.' By weaving Christian values throughout our curriculum and partnering with parents, we help children develop a strong moral compass and a faithful commitment to unlocking their unique, God-given talents.
LOVE (1 John 3:18 – 'My children, our love should not be just words and talk: it must be true love, which shows itself in action.')
As a Christian family, we believe love must show itself in action (1 John 3:18). We practice this daily by providing an enriched curriculum that encourages every child to reach their full potential. Supporting our pupils to 'Reach for the Stars' is our ultimate practical demonstration of Christ-like love.
JOY (Romans 12:12 – 'Let your heart keep you joyful, be patient in your troubles and pray at all times.')
We believe education should bring deep delight. Our vision of a happy school family where children are excited about learning directly aligns with Romans 12:12. By providing a stimulating environment, we foster a joyful curiosity and a prayerful resilience, helping our pupils look at the world with hope and enthusiasm.

St Andrew’s Admissions
All parents wanting to apply for a place for a child at St Andrew’s primary school are expected to take a tour of the school.
If you’re a prospective parent and haven’t had a school tour yet, please click the button below for the next available dates and to book a place on a tour.
During your tour we will tell you everything you need to know about the school, answer your questions and explain how Lambeth schools’ application system and selection criteria works. At the end of the tour we will cover all the information you need to know about how to apply for a place in Reception at St Andrew’s.
And, if you’re looking for our step-by step guide on ‘How to apply for primary school in Lambeth’, please click the button below.
Are you interested in joining the St. Andrew’s family?
St Andrew’s is a Church of England school, but we are an inclusive school that welcomes all learners regardless of race, gender, and ethnicity or religion, stage of English learning, ability, special educational needs or impairments.
In the event that we are oversubscribed, our Governing body has designated that the majority of available places be made available to regular worshippers at St Andrew’s church. To download a copy of the full selection criteria click the button below.
However, we are proud of the values that underpin our Christian school and encourage applications from all faiths.
St Andrew’s has a single form entry with a maximum class size of 30 children in Reception. Our aim is to retain our ‘small school feeling’, deeply rooted in the local community, and as such we will always try to accommodate applications from local parents.
When to apply for a Reception place at Lambeth primary schools
Children join our primary school in September of the school year in which they are five – so, for entry in September 2026, this applies to children born between 1 September 2021 and 31 August 2022.
The closing date for applications for a Reception class place at a primary school in the 2026/27 academic year is midnight on 15th January 2026.
If your application is received after 15th January 2026, it will be considered a late application by Lambeth Council and will not be considered for a place until after 16th April 2026 (the date that all applicants are notified). Missing the 15th January deadline will therefore significantly reduce your chance of getting a place at St Andrew’s as your preferred choice.
How to apply for a primary school Reception place at St Andrew’s
We have prepared a ‘step-by-step’ guide on how to apply for a primary school place in Lambeth using the online Common Application Form. Please click here to use that guide.
The admissions system for all Reception age children is managed by the local authority in which you live and not by St Andrew’s directly. For most parents applying for a place at St Andrew’s that will mean applying through Lambeth Council.
However, for a place at St Andrew’s, all parents are required to apply using the Lambeth application system and submit a simple additional application form direct to St Andrew’s.
To apply through Lambeth Council, all parents are required to fill out a Common Application Form (‘CAF’) for their child, preferably using the online Lambeth e-admissions process, which is the Primary Schools Admissions Portal.
Parents who live in other boroughs may apply for places in a Lambeth school, but must apply through their home borough which will then be passed to Lambeth Council.
Lambeth Council provides a comprehensive Primary Schools Admission Booklet that details the Reception place application process that you can download below.
Once you have completed the CAF (for Lambeth or your borough), you’ll need to complete the short St Andrew’s application.
You can download this below and then post it or drop it into the school office - addressed to Applications, St. Andrew's CE Primary School, Kay Road, London, SW9 9DE - or email a scanned copy to admin@standrewsce.lambeth.sch.uk

Art and Design
We value the creative curriculum and believe that it can have a powerful and positive effect on children, helping them to become confident, creative learners who are able to express their individual interests, thoughts and ideas.
We believe that a high-quality art and design education should engage, inspire and challenge pupils, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art, craft and design.
We encourage children to learn from and be inspired by the work of great artists from different cultures and understand the contribution art has made to society, both past and present.
As pupils progress, we support them to be able to think critically and develop a more rigorous understanding of art and design.
Through art work in the classroom, the children have the opportunity to develop their skills in drawing, textiles, sculpture, painting, print making and collage.
These areas are developed continuously throughout the school from the early years through to year six and the children have the opportunity to revisit skills from previous years before learning new ones.
Developing skills in drawing is given a high status and children are encouraged to draw not only in art lessons, but across the curriculum.
We encourage children to express individuality in their work and to keep their own personalised sketch books where they can explore ideas, be inventive and take risks.
Click image to enlarge
How do we plan and teach Art and Design?
At least one art project is taught per term in each class. Teachers plan sequences of lessons that will build on and develop the children’s skills culminating in a final piece.
The skills and knowledge that children will develop throughout each art topic are mapped across each year group and across the school to ensure progression.
The emphasis on knowledge ensures that children understand the context of the artwork, as well as the artists that they are learning about and being inspired by.
This enables links to other curriculum areas, with the children developing a considerable knowledge of individual artists and individual works.
Children are given opportunities to express their creative imagination, as well as practise and develop mastery in the key processes of art: drawing, painting, printing, textiles, collage and sculpture.
Whole school project work – ‘Take One Artist’ ensures that art is given high status in the curriculum and at the beginning of each academic year we choose one artist to study in depth across the federation of schools.
Trips to art galleries and exhibitions are carried out to enhance the children’s learning experiences and deepen their understanding and knowledge.
Click here to view our ART & DESIGN CURRICULUM MAP
How we evaluate learning in Art and Design
The impact of our art curriculum can clearly been seen in the children’s sketchbooks which pass on with them to the following year group.
At the beginning of each unit, a detailed overview outlines the main learning objective alongside the skills that the children will build on and those which will follow.
The opportunity to evaluate and reflect on the learning is planned for towards the end of the unit to enable the children to see how their learning is progressing and where they need to take it next.
On completion of the unit of work, key assessment targets are identified and the children are able to self-assess against them.
Class teachers then use the children’s research and preparatory work, along with the final piece in order to make a judgement as to whether each child is working towards, at or above the expected level.
